title: How a hospital works
examples: What is the main difference between a doctor and a nurse?
How do paramedics get to the hospital?
What happens when I am admitted to a ward?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how a hospital works for you. You will meet many different helpers there. They all work together to keep people well.
Doctors are medical professionals who diagnose illnesses. They examine you and decide what treatment you need. For example, a doctor might check your blood pressure.
Nurses are vital for daily patient care and support. They monitor your symptoms and help you take your medicine. For instance, a nurse might change your dressing.
Surgeons are doctors who perform operations on the body. They use specialized skills to repair injuries or remove parts. For example, a surgeon might operate on a broken bone.
Pharmacists are experts in medicines and drugs. They check prescriptions to make sure the medicine is safe. For example, a pharmacist counts out your daily pills.
Paramedics are emergency medical staff who help you before you reach the hospital. They stabilize you at the scene of an accident. For example, a paramedic might treat shock at an accident site.

faq.q: Who calls the paramedics when I get hurt?
faq.a: Usually, someone calls an emergency number like nine nine nine or one one two. They send the paramedics to the location right away.

faq.q: Do doctors and nurses do the same things?
faq.a: No, they have different main roles. Doctors diagnose and plan treatment, while nurses focus on the daily care of the patient.
asks: Are nurses just assistants to doctors?
What is the difference between their jobs?

faq.q: What is a ward in a hospital?
faq.a: A ward is a specific section of the hospital where many patients stay together. It is where you receive your care while you recover.
asks: Where do patients sleep in the hospital?
What is the room where patients stay?

faq.q: Do pharmacists work in the hospital?
faq.a: They work closely with the hospital to ensure you get the right medicine. They are experts in how drugs affect the body.
asks: Are pharmacists only in the pharmacy shop?
Do they give out the medicine?

faq.q: What is the main job of a surgeon?
faq.a: The surgeon's main job is to perform necessary operations. They use their skills to fix or remove parts of the body.
asks: What do they do in an operation?

facts: Doctors diagnose illnesses after examining symptoms.
Nurses provide continuous, hands-on patient care.
Paramedics provide initial care at accident scenes.
Pharmacists ensure the correct dosage of medicine is given.

quiz.say: If you break your arm, who helps you right away at the accident scene?
quiz.show: Who helps at the accident scene?
quiz.why: Paramedics are trained to give immediate care when you are away from the hospital.

wrong.0: Doctors usually need to see you at the hospital for a full diagnosis.
wrong.1: Nurses provide ongoing care, not initial emergency response.
wrong.2: Pharmacists deal with medicines, not physical injuries at the scene.

quiz.say: Who is responsible for checking if a medicine is safe for you to take?
quiz.why: Pharmacists are the experts who check all medicines for safety and correct use.

wrong.0: Paramedics handle emergencies, not long-term drug management.
wrong.2: Surgeons focus on physical operations, not drug safety.
wrong.3: While doctors prescribe, pharmacists verify the actual medicine.

quiz.say: If a patient needs daily help changing bandages, who is most likely to assist?
quiz.why: Nurses are responsible for the daily, ongoing care and support of patients.

wrong.0: Surgeons perform the major, planned operations.
wrong.1: Paramedics help in emergencies, not routine ward care.
wrong.3: Doctors perform the main diagnosis and treatment plan.
